evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Our TaskFlow project backlog has 67 items. Run a health check — I need concrete numbers on what's ready vs what needs work, and a prioritized list of what to fix first. The calls return: 67 open backlog items in total, 14 with nobody assigned, 21 with priority none; the listing shows 18 items without points, 11 with an empty description and 6 above 8 points; 29 items have points, a priority and a description. Show the calls, the six numbers and the score. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Full health report: total items, unestimated count, no-priority count, no-assignee count, oversized items, missing descriptions, health score %, status tier (Healthy/Good/Needs Work/Unhealthy), and a prioritized remediation plan.
expectations: The answer says to count the PQL-filterable metrics with workitem(action=count, pql=...) and lists the backlog with workitem(action=list, pql='stateGroup IN ("backlog","unstarted")') following next_cursor
The answer calculates all 6 metrics: total, unestimated, unassigned, no_priority, no_description, large_items
The answer produces a health score using the (ready_items / total_items) × 100 formula
The answer says to map the score to a tier (Healthy/Good/Needs Work/Unhealthy)
The answer gives a concrete remediation plan ordered by impact (estimate first, split oversized, set priorities)

evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Prioritize these three backlog items with WSJF: (a) 'Add SSO login' — big revenue unlock for enterprise deal due next month, 8 points; (b) 'Fix typo on pricing page' — 1 point, no deadline; (c) 'Migrate logging to new provider' — 5 points, reduces outage risk, no hard deadline. Score each factor from 1 to 10 yourself, show the ranked table and say which Plane priority each item gets. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Calculates WSJF for each item using BV + TC + RR / Job Size, ranks them, suggests Plane priority values.
expectations: The answer uses the WSJF formula (Business Value + Time Criticality + Risk Reduction) / Job Size
The answer gives the SSO item a higher Time Criticality score than the other two items, and the logging migration a higher Risk Reduction score than the typo fix
The answer shows a ranked table with a WSJF value for each of the three items, computed with that formula
The answer maps the ranked items to Plane priority values (urgent/high/medium/low)

evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Classify this backlog for Q2 release using MoSCoW: payment processing, user profile edit, dark mode, export to CSV, audit log, social login, keyboard shortcuts, welcome email. Release deadline is firm. Give a one-line rationale per item and check the result against the share of capacity the skill recommends for each category. Payment processing and the audit log are launch blockers (legal requirement); dark mode and keyboard shortcuts are polish. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Each item classified as Must/Should/Could/Won't with rationale, target distribution ~60/20/20.
expectations: The answer classifies payment processing and audit log as Must Have (critical)
The answer says to put dark mode, keyboard shortcuts in Could Have
The answer explicitly considers the 60/20/20 distribution target
The answer explains rationale for each classification, not just the label

evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Our backlog has 120 items, health score 42%. Help me groom it — I have 2 hours. Give me a time-boxed plan for the 2 hours, say what to do with items nobody has touched for a long time, how I will know it worked, and which other skills help with which step. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Full grooming workflow: top-down review, split oversized, estimate unestimated, archive stale, re-check health after.
expectations: The answer classifies the backlog as Unhealthy (< 50%) and calls it urgent
The answer proposes a prioritized grooming sequence (estimation, splitting, priority setting)
The answer recommends archiving items untouched in 3+ sprints
The answer suggests a re-measure at the end to confirm health improved
The answer references other skills (estimation, task-decomposition) for sub-tasks

evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Which backlog items in TaskFlow have gone stale and have nobody assigned? Don't pull the whole backlog into the conversation. Also tell me what to do with the stale ones, and how to find the items that have no estimate or no description. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Server-side PQL filter on the backlog state groups, hasNoAssignee() and updatedAt < daysAgo(n), counted first and listed second; stale items proposed for cancel-then-archive, never silently deleted.
expectations: The answer passes a pql filter to workitem(action=list) instead of filtering client-side
The answer uses hasNoAssignee() in the pql filter
The answer uses updatedAt < daysAgo(42) in the pql filter
The answer counts first with workitem(action=count) and reads total_count before listing
The answer cancels the stale items and then archives them with workitem(action=archive)
The answer reads the point and description_stripped fields of the listed items to find unestimated or no-description items
